title: Wire the static Development Monitor as an opt-in Actions artifact

requirement.summary: Continue the reviewed ADR-0009 product loop by adding a minimal, explicitly dispatched GitHub Actions path that renders the existing static Development Monitor from validated portable inputs and uploads only the self-contained HTML read model.

objective.rationale: The local Monitor and redacted export contracts are implemented; the next bounded product slice is an honest, human-opted-in Actions artifact without widening governance or Git authority.

goal: Extend only the future 0.3 managed governance workflow template with an explicit manual-dispatch option that builds and uploads a source-limited Development Monitor HTML artifact.
non_goals: Do not publish AgentGov 0.3, change the stable integration default, migrate a consumer, or claim that an unpublished development wheel exists.
Do not upload local .agentgov state, raw event files, a development export bundle, source content, validation output, credentials, or absolute paths.
Do not overwrite an existing workflow, add automatic push or pull-request Monitor upload, or grant Git, pull-request, merge, release, deployment, or production authority.
Do not add exception records, action-loop self-reporting, cross-stage discovery claims, GitHub Pages, telemetry, hooks, or a daemon.
acceptance_signals: Only a caller-supplied, digest-pinned 0.3-or-newer managed governance workflow gains the Monitor artifact path; stable 0.1 and 0.2 rendered workflows remain unchanged.
Monitor publication defaults to false and runs only after an explicit workflow_dispatch boolean input.
The workflow passes an explicit redacted export to AgentGov when supplied and otherwise uses ci_only; combined is selected only when both the export and CI event files are present.
AgentGov remains responsible for rejecting a non-redacted export or any non-CI actor in a CI event store.
The artifact contains only the self-contained Monitor HTML and never uploads the input export, raw events, .agentgov directory, source content, or validation output.
The governance workflow retains read-only permissions, pinned actions, disabled checkout credentials, and no secret or write-permission references.
Focused workflow and documentation tests plus the complete repository suite pass.

items: An Actions artifact could imply CI observed local development that was never explicitly exported.
A broad upload path could disclose the redacted input bundle or local event files instead of only the derived Monitor.
Rendering an unpublished version into a live workflow could create a false executable or release identity.

stop_conditions: Stop if the workflow must reference an unpublished wheel URL or fabricated digest.
Stop if the Monitor cannot distinguish explicit exported_development, actor-validated ci_only, and combined inputs.
Stop if implementation requires automatic transfer of local state or any repository write permission.
Stop if an existing consumer workflow would need to be modified without a separate release and migration decision.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly authorized the next bounded work item after reviewing its scope, non-goals, acceptance signals, and packaging stop boundary. The delivered task was paused on 2026-08-05 to remove it from automatic discovery; this is routing hygiene, not a claim of semantic completion, acceptance, merge, or release.
